findings.title: SPF exceeds the 10 DNS lookup limit

detection_methods.prior_justification: the count is computed from records we fetched ourselves, but include chains change often and a chain we could not finish walking returns inconclusive

evidence.label: TXT at paytm.com

records: v=spf1 ip4:13.127.134.11 ip4:54.240.85.29 ip4:54.240.85.30 include:amazonses.com include:_include1.paytm.com include:_include2.paytm.com include:_spf.salesforce.com include:_spf.google.com include:servers.mcsv.net include:email.onedirect.in include:email-messaging.com -all

evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

record.raw: v=spf1 ip4:13.127.134.11 ip4:54.240.85.29 ip4:54.240.85.30 include:amazonses.com include:_include1.paytm.com include:_include2.paytm.com include:_spf.salesforce.com include:_spf.google.com include:servers.mcsv.net include:email.onedirect.in include:email-messaging.com -all

v=spf1 include:_spf.one97.net include:amazonses.com include:_include3.paytm.com include:_onenine7.paytm.com ip4:125.19.44.66/32 ip4:125.21.245.156/32 ip4:13.232.157.69/32 ip4:13.232.105.32/32 ip4:13.126.236.121/32 ip4:13.232.146.80/32 -all

problems: include loop: amazonses.com is already in the chain
include loop: _spf.google.com is already in the chain

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8

records: v=spf1 ip4:13.127.134.11 ip4:54.240.85.29 ip4:54.240.85.30 include:amazonses.com include:_include1.paytm.com include:_include2.paytm.com include:_spf.salesforce.com include:_spf.google.com include:servers.mcsv.net include:email.onedirect.in include:email-messaging.com -all

evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: Evaluating this SPF policy needs 18 DNS lookups, above the limit of 10 in RFC 7208 section 4.6.4. The chain is: paytm.com (8) -> amazonses.com (0) -> _include1.paytm.com (4) -> _include2.paytm.com (0) -> _spf.salesforce.com (1) -> _spf.google.com (0) -> servers.mcsv.net (0) -> email.onedirect.in (0) -> email-messaging.com (1) -> _spf.one97.net (1) -> _include3.paytm.com (1) -> _onenine7.paytm.com (0) -> spf1.email-messaging.com (0) -> _include4.paytm.com (1) -> 910033d5.ppspf.net (1).
findings.impact: Receivers stop evaluating and return permerror, so SPF fails for this domain entirely. Legitimate mail can be rejected and forged mail is not caught.
findings.remediation: Reduce the chain below ten lookups. The usual fix is to replace include: terms for providers you no longer use, and to flatten a provider's ranges into ip4:/ip6: terms - those cost no lookups at all.

findings.title: DMARC uses relaxed alignment

detection_methods.prior_justification: the adkim= and aspf= tags are read directly, and default to relaxed

evidence.label: TXT at _dmarc.paytm.com
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: DMARC alignment is relaxed (adkim=r, aspf=r). Relaxed alignment accepts any subdomain of paytm.com in the authenticated identifier.
findings.impact: Relaxed alignment is the default and is appropriate for most senders. It does mean that anyone able to publish records under a subdomain can pass DMARC for the parent.
findings.remediation: If every legitimate sender signs and sends as the exact domain, set adkim=s and aspf=s. If subdomains send mail, relaxed is the correct setting and no change is needed.

findings.title: DKIM key is below 2048 bits

detection_methods.prior_justification: the modulus length is measured from the key itself; every common selector is read, but a domain may publish others we cannot find

evidence.label: TXT at google._domainkey.paytm.com
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: DKIM keys below 2048 bits are published at google._domainkey.paytm.com (1024 bits) and default._domainkey.paytm.com (1024 bits) and s2._domainkey.paytm.com (1024 bits). Each meets the RFC 8301 minimum of 1024 bits, below the recommended 2048. The domain also publishes k2._domainkey.paytm.com, s1._domainkey.paytm.com. We cannot tell from DNS which selector it signs its mail with. RFC 6376 section 6.1.2 has a verifier fetch the key named by the signature's s= tag, so a signature may name any selector the domain publishes, the weaker one included.
findings.impact: This is a margin, not a break: RFC 8301 permits the key, and recommends 2048 bits for signers. Moving to 2048 bits brings the domain in line with that recommendation.
findings.remediation: If a weaker selector is no longer used for signing, remove its record. Otherwise generate a new 2048-bit key with your mail provider, publish it under a new selector, switch signing to it, and remove the old selector once no mail is signed with it.

findings.title: No MTA-STS policy published

detection_methods.prior_justification: a definite TXT answer at _mta-sts with no v=STSv1 term is direct observation

evidence.label: TXT at _mta-sts.paytm.com
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: No MTA-STS policy record is published at _mta-sts.paytm.com.
findings.impact: Without MTA-STS a sending server that cannot negotiate TLS will deliver mail in plaintext rather than refusing, so an attacker positioned on the network can strip encryption and read the message.
findings.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _mta-sts.paytm.com of the form 'v=STSv1; id=<timestamp>', and serve the matching policy file at https://mta-sts.paytm.com/.well-known/mta-sts.txt. Start the policy in mode: testing, then move to mode: enforce.

findings.title: No SMTP TLS reporting configured

detection_methods.prior_justification: a definite TXT answer at _smtp._tls with no v=TLSRPTv1 term is direct observation

evidence.label: TXT at _smtp._tls.paytm.com
evidence.control_rationale: a random-label probe in the same zone; without it a wildcard would make every lookup under this domain appear to succeed

evidence.label: independent re-query via 8.8.8.8
evidence.control_rationale: the control for this re-query is the first resolver's answer, captured above

findings.description: No SMTP TLS reporting record is published at _smtp._tls.paytm.com.
findings.impact: Nobody is told when a sending server fails to establish TLS to your mail servers, so a downgrade attack or a broken certificate goes unnoticed.
findings.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _smtp._tls.paytm.com of the form 'v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls-reports@paytm.com'.
